historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: RDDT has only 4 fiscal years of history (IPO Mar-2024) and EPS/equity/owner-FCF all flip sign across the period (losses through FY2023-24, profitable FY2025), so standard CAGRs on EPS, equity and FCF are not meaningful/comparable. Revenue is the only cleanly positive, comparable series and is used as the primary historical growth anchor. FY2024 owner FCF is further distorted by a one-time ~$595M IPO RSU cliff-vest SBC charge and a $189.9M one-off equity-settlement tax payment, both excluded from the projection base (TTM Jul-2025-Jun-2026 used instead).
historical_growth.notes: SBC-adjusted (owner) FCF only turned durably positive in FY2025 ($150.3M, 6.8% margin) and has since scaled sharply to $505.0M TTM (18.2% margin) through H1-2026 operating leverage -- this is a genuine margin inflection, not a comparable multi-year CAGR base. Reported FCF materially overstates the cash generated for shareholders in every year: FY2025 reported FCF of $684.2M becomes $150.3M owner FCF once SBC+withholding ($447.2M) and interest income ($86.7M) are stripped -- 78% of reported FCF was SBC/interest, not owner cash flow.

memo_sbc_noncash.description: If SBC were treated as a non-cash expense with zero economic cost to shareholders (i.e., added back to owner FCF rather than deducted), base-case intrinsic value would be:
memo_sbc_noncash.interpretation: The ~$46/share spread (26% of the base-case IV) is the honest measure of how much of Reddit's valuation depends on how SBC is treated. Given RDDT has no buyback program, this spread is real -- shareholders bear the dilution as future SBC-driven share issuance is uncovered.

sanity_check_verdict.reason: Weighted IV $160.67 vs $153.95 (+4.4%), rebuilt on Q2-2026 actuals.
sanity_check_verdict.nuance: The scenario spread is very wide -- bull $247.81 to bear $80.14 -- because a 10-year model on a company four years past IPO is mostly terminal value. Treat the base as a central estimate with low confidence, not a target. The near-term operating momentum is not in doubt; the decade of compounding is.
sanity_check_verdict.value_investor_conclusion: Roughly fairly valued at +4.4%. Executing well, net cash, no debt -- but the prior +26.9% was an artefact of a decade of hypergrowth extrapolation off a stale base. No margin of safety at $153.95.

fields_updated: full model rebuild on Q2-2026 actuals

valuation_philosophy: Rebuilt 2026-08-28 on Q2-2026. Unusually for this session's audits, the prior model was too CONSERVATIVE on the near term and too aggressive on the far term at the same time. Its $505.0m FY2025 base with +44% Year-1 growth implied FY2026 FCF of $727m; H1-2026 alone delivered $572.5m, or 78.7% of it. Q2 FCF was $260.7m against $110.8m (+135%) on revenue of $804.9m (+61.1% YoY), with DAUq 130.3m (+18%) and ARPU $6.18 (+36%). So the base year is rebased upward to $1,145.0m -- H1 doubled at FLAT seasonality, deliberately declining the H2 uplift Reddit's ad seasonality would justify. But the prior model then ran 44/36/29/23/18/15/13/12/11/10 for a decade off that smaller base, which compounds a hypergrowth rate far longer than any advertising platform has sustained. Rebased with a faster decay (20% falling to 7%), the weighted IV FALLS from $195.32 to $160.67 even though near-term cash flow is running well ahead. The bigger base does not offset the shorter runway. Net cash of ~$2.8bn and no debt. Reddit is genuinely executing; the question is only what a decade of that execution is worth today.
